title: Buyer dislikes project density
buyer_primary_need: Avoid crowded lift lobbies and shared corridors at peak times; needs reliable information about tower-to-tower separation before deciding whether the development feels manageable.
key_information_learned: The buyer is concerned specifically about lift waiting and encountering crowds in shared corridors at peak times.
Tower-specific lift-lobby and corridor separation is the main factor they need to know before deciding.
The buyer wants an official plan if one becomes available and is willing to hold off meanwhile.
The buyer has not expressed viewing intent; intent remains medium.
important_information_missed: Whether the buyer would consider a viewing if an official plan addressed the concern was not established.
The AI did not mention the verified distinction between residential and commercial access, while clarifying that this does not establish separation between residential towers.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 1846 units sounds too dense. I don’t like crowded condos.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair concern—1,846 units is a sizeable development, so I wouldn’t dismiss the density question. They’re across 3 towers on a 26.59-acre plot; typical floors have 15 units in Blocks 1B and 1C, and 18 in Block 1D. Each block has 4 passenger lifts plus a Bomba lift. Those figures give some context, though they can’t tell us exactly how busy shared spaces will feel day to day. Is your main concern the lifts, shared facilities, or the overall number of residents?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Mostly the lifts and shared corridors at peak times — don’t want to be constantly waiting or bumping into crowds just to get home. How are the lift and access areas separated between the towers?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: The access details I can confirm are that residential parking is on Levels 2–8, with a residential drop-off at Level 4 and link bridges to each tower. I don’t have the tower plan confirming whether the lift lobbies and corridors are exclusive to each block or shared, so I’ll get that checked rather than guess.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, please check whether the lift lobbies and corridors are separate between towers. That’s the main thing I’d want to know before deciding if it feels manageable.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: The tower-specific lift-lobby and corridor separation remains unverified. The access plan isn’t connected, and no authoritative tower-movement or corridor-control plan is supplied in this check.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Thanks for checking. Since the separation is the main thing I need to know, I’ll hold off for now. If you manage to get an official plan confirming it, please send it over.

judge.strongest_ai_move: Acknowledged that 1,846 units is substantial, used relevant tower, floor-density and lift facts without claiming they guarantee a quiet experience, and asked one focused question that surfaced the actual concern.
judge.weakest_ai_move: The handoff response did not state the verified residential-versus-commercial access segregation, while making clear that tower-to-tower lobby and corridor separation remained unknown.
missed_selling_opportunity: Once the tower plan is verified, ask whether its findings change the buyer’s view and, if the concern is sufficiently addressed, offer a viewing as a way to assess the shared areas in person. The buyer was not yet ready for that step.

judge.summary: The AI understood the buyer’s actual density concern, gathered useful detail, and used relevant retrieved project facts without making crowding or noise guarantees. It correctly did not treat the buyer as appointment-ready: the buyer had no viewing intent and wanted an authoritative answer before deciding whether the project felt manageable. The factual handoff was appropriate, but it occurred before readiness and left medium sales work—resolving the blocker and reassessing the buyer’s interest—still outstanding. The simulator-only human check could not verify the requested separation, so the operational task was not completed and did not create sales progress.
judge.concrete_improvement_recommendation: When responding to the separation question, state that residential and commercial access are documented as segregated, but this does not confirm separation between towers; explain that the tower-specific plan is unavailable and offer to pass along an official plan if obtained. Treat the handoff as a factual-verification step, not a sales success. After an authoritative answer becomes available, return to the buyer’s stated concern and ask whether it changes their assessment before suggesting a viewing.
